answer.text:
VAT IDs and legal entity names must be validated at the point of capture to ensure the correct application of VAT. This prevents both GitLab and its customers from being confronted with incorrect (non-recoverable) VAT, as an invalid or mismatched VAT ID can result in VAT liability, interest, and penalties for GitLab that are rarely recoverable from the customer afterwards [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#why-this-exists].

The specific criteria for when VAT validation applies are:

- The Account Type must be "Prospect"
- The Account billing country must be anything other than the United States or Canada

If either of these conditions is not met, no validation is required and no banner appears. This requirement is not driven by the opportunity's Subscription Type, but by Account status. Domestic deals (US and Canada) are excluded [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#phase-1-criteria-for-when-vat-validation-applies].

Validation process on quotes:

- Validation is performed in Salesforce using Fonoa:
  - The VAT/Tax ID field is entered by the sales rep.
  - The VAT Validation Status is set by the system after a Fonoa check.
  - The Legal Entity Validation Status is set by the system (Tool-Verified) or can be manually set by the AE (Sales Rep-Verified) or Sales Ops (Sales Ops-Verified) after confirming the name with the customer [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#field-reference][sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#things-to-watch].

- The submission is ready for approval only when:
  - VAT Validation Status is Valid, and
  - Legal Entity Validation Status is Tool-Verified, Sales Rep-Verified, or Sales Ops-Verified [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#step-6-submitting-for-approval].

- The Account Name must exactly match the registered legal entity name returned by Fonoa (including suffixes, punctuation, and capitalization). The Account Name is the Sold-To legal entity name, not a trading/brand/parent name. "Mark as Verified" should only be used after actual confirmation with the customer [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#things-to-watch].

- Validation must be completed before creating a quote. If a quote is created before validation, the VAT ID may be missing from the billing account, leading to incorrect tax calculation [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#things-to-watch].

- On "Closed Won" and "Send to Zuora" in Salesforce, the validated Account Name and VAT ID flow to Zuora for billing and tax purposes [sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#step-8-order-form-and-downstream-systems].

Owner: @jrabbits (Field Operations)

Sources:
- [VAT ID and Legal Entity Name Validation – Why this exists](sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#why-this-exists)
- [VAT ID and Legal Entity Name Validation – Phase 1 criteria](sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#phase-1-criteria-for-when-vat-validation-applies)
- [VAT ID and Legal Entity Name Validation – Field reference](sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#field-reference)
- [VAT ID and Legal Entity Name Validation – Things to watch](sales/field-operations/vat-id-legal-entity-validation#things-to-watch)

nodes.label: How are VAT IDs and legal entity names validated on quotes?
VAT ID and Legal Entity Name Validation
Why this exists
nodes.text:
GitLab validates the customer's VAT ID and registered legal entity name at the point of capture, so that the invoice applies the correct VAT. As a result, both GitLab as well as our customers are not confronted with incorrect (non-recoverable) VAT.

**Why is a valid VAT ID number of the Sold To legal entity important?**

- For GitLab: an invalid or mismatched VAT ID means VAT should have been charged but wasn't. That becomes GitLab's liability, with interest and penalties, and is rarely recoverable from the customer afterwards.
- For the customer: an invoice with an incorrect VAT ID or address is not a valid tax invoice in most jurisdictions, so they cannot reclaim the input VAT; the invoice

nodes.label: Step 6 — Submitting for approval
nodes.text:
The submission is ready for **Submit for Approval**. The submission passes when:

- VAT Validation Status is Valid, **and**
- Legal Entity Validation Status is Tool-Verified, Sales Rep-Verified or Sales Ops-Verified

With both satisfied, the submission proceeds with no additional prompt.

![The account fields once validation is complete](/images/sales/field-operations/vat-id-validation/account-fields-complete.png)

nodes.label: Step 8 — Order form and downstream systems
nodes.text:
The order form displays the sold-to legal entity name and the VAT ID from the Account.

On "Closed Won" and "Send to Zuora" attributes in Salesforce, the Account Name populates the Zuora billing account name. The validated VAT ID flows to the Zuora VAT ID field. Tax rules read the VAT ID at billing-account level, which is why the Account must be correct before the quote is sent.

The billing account is created within Zuora at the end of the Salesforce validation sequence, illustrated as follows:

Account → Opportunity → Quote → Quote Approval → Opportunity Approval → Closed Won → Quote Sent to Zuora → Billing Account

nodes.label: Field reference
nodes.text:
The following fields are retained in the Account, under **Other Account Info**, beside the existing VAT/Tax ID field.

| Field | Populated by | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VAT/Tax ID | You | The customer's VAT or tax identification number. |
| VAT Validation Status | System | Result of the Fonoa check. See Step 3. |
| VAT Last Validated Date | System | Timestamp of the most recent validation attempt. |
| Legal Entity Validation Status | System, or the AE via Mark as Verified | Result of the name comparison. See Step 3. |
| Legal Entity Validation Date | System | Timestamp of the most recent legal entity determination. |

Both status fields are **read-only for Sales**. Edit access is limite

nodes.text:
